prompt: Should bank managers be asked to own shares of their
response: institution? A company owned by its management would likely operate less efficiently than one whose management answers only to shareholders. In addition, management-owned firms have worse financial performance and are less likely to innovate than shareholder-controlled firms. But shareholder-owned firms face many types of problems that require management intervention, particularly those dealing with moral hazard and the allocation of excess profits to top management teams. One solution is for top management teams and board members at shareholder-controlled companies to own non-controlled equity, a proposal first put forward decades ago by Robert Shiller and which we propose here—with some modifications—for banks today. We investigate our proposal using data from all banks in Europe with a long (over ten years) history of shareholder capital structure from pre-crisis banking and apply our proposed model to evaluate its effects on management incentives before and during the financial crisis. Our results show that shareholder capital structure leads to lower incentive-free earnings and non-contractible performance with negative effects on innovation and less positive effects on moral hazard.

Data Accuracy and Timeliness in Official Statistics for Global Development
Abstract
We explore the interconnections between two pressing issues for official statistics systems worldwide. A priority has long been increasing timely release of data and reliability or quality improvements. There is also a growing need to expand from conventional statistics systems to provide more holistic or integrated indicators and indicators with regional disaggregations in support of United Nations (UN) sustainable development goals (SDGs). This proposal seeks to analyze the interrelated dynamics of these two challenges through case studies covering five countries and three regions. The primary aim is to provide insights into how both data and indicators management systems adapt to contextually different regional and environmental issues while demonstrating the importance of information availability and performance indicators as a resource for evidence-based decision making about national statistics programs and governance.
